outcome: Give hotel gm / hospitality revenue director a governed method to improve incremental guest satisfaction by cohort using stay preferences, opt-in records and service history, with final decisions…
overview: Guest Personalisation with Consent addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in hospitality and tourism operations. The first proof of value uses stay preferences, opt-in records and service history. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is incremental guest satisfaction by cohort, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: stay preferences, opt-in records and service history; define incremental guest satisfaction by cohort and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hotel GM / Hospitality Revenue Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for incremental guest satisfaction by cohort
